xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2989: State-branch push runs under the per-issue record lock — a stalled push starves verdict journal writes (8+ min observed)

plan.title: State-branch push runs under the per-issue record lock — a stalled push starves verdict journal writes (8+ min observed)
plan.author: agent:k3

narratives.Problem: updateIssueRecord (src/lib/pan-dir/record-update.ts:208) holds the per-issue fs lock across flushAutoCommits AND reconcileStatePush; a stalled git push held the PAN-806 lock 8+ minutes on 2026-07-21, starving a review-passed verdict write past its ~1s retry budget into the workspace pipeline-verdict.json fallback. Compounding defects: nothing ever folds back or deletes the fallback file (canonical journal lagged ~1h), and the dashboard server inherits OVERDECK_AGENT_ID=deploy-patrol from deploy-patrol's pan reload child (src/cli/commands/restart.ts:182 passthrough), so every lock-owner string misattributes server writes.
narratives.Proposal: Three independent fixes (operator-verified direction in the issue comment): (1) bound the under-lock durability wait with a shared deadline (OVERDECK_RECORD_DURABILITY_BUDGET_MS, default 30s) that throws a typed RecordDurabilityTimeoutError, skips restore-on-timeout, and never aborts peers' shared-gitRoot flushes; (2) scrub OVERDECK_AGENT_ID/OVERDECK_ISSUE_ID/OVERDECK_SESSION_TYPE from the spawned dashboard server env, preserving the inherited identity as OVERDECK_DASHBOARD_SPAWNED_BY for the PAN-2322 port guard; (3) proactively drain the workspace verdict fallback (drainWorkspaceVerdictFallback + unref'd 5s/30s/120s retries), deleting the file once the journal is at least as new.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No lock TTL or steal-with-audit path (breaks mutual exclusion; PAN-1791-class corruption risk)
- No restructuring of the under-lock flush; the durability-ordering invariant stands
- No change to RECORD_LOCK_RETRY_DELAYS_MS (~1s contender budget)
- No change to the flush's own 60s bound or per-git 30s timeouts (OVERDECK_STATE_FLUSH_TIMEOUT_MS / OVERDECK_STATE_PUSH_TIMEOUT_MS)
- No drain on the status-read path; reads keep overlay semantics
- No retry-budget increase or re-drive logic for updateIssueRecordForIssue callers beyond the drain triggers

autoDecisions.summary: Deadline race (30s default, env-tunable) around flush+reconcile instead of restructuring the lock scope
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue comment names the bounded hold as 'the smaller correct change'; the under-lock flush is deliberate for durability ordering (record-update.ts:220-222).
The mutation may still land via the un-aborted background flush; rewinding to the pre-mutation snapshot could clobber a concurrently-landing commit.
The signal path aborts ALL active flushes for the shared state-worktree gitRoot (abortAndSettleGitRoot, auto-commit.ts:463); one writer's timeout must not kill peers' commits.

autoDecisions.summary: Relocate inherited OVERDECK_AGENT_ID to OVERDECK_DASHBOARD_SPAWNED_BY rather than plain deletion
autoDecisions.rationale: The PAN-2322 port-override guard legitimately needs the spawner identity (conv-* exempt, pipeline-role refused, absent allowed); relocating preserves its decision table exactly while making record-lock owner strings truthful.

autoDecisions.summary: Drain triggers live in review-status-record-sync.ts (successful write + scheduled retries), not an fs-lock release hook
autoDecisions.rationale: A generic lock-release callback couples the records domain to the verdict domain; the chosen triggers satisfy 'drain proactively' without that coupling, and reads already overlay the fallback so a stranded fallback is cosmetic lag, not corruption.
Stealing a live lock breaks the read-modify-write mutual exclusion that prevents lost updates (PAN-1791); bounding the hold relieves starvation without corruption risk.

items.title: Bound the under-lock durability wait in updateIssueRecord

expected_outputs: record-update-durability-budget.test.ts passes (timeout, no-restore, env-override, and no-regression cases)

narrative.Action: In src/lib/pan-dir/record-update.ts: add RecordDurabilityTimeoutError, recordDurabilityBudgetMs() (env OVERDECK_RECORD_DURABILITY_BUDGET_MS, default 30000), and withRecordDurabilityDeadline() (Promise.race against a shared deadline; NO AbortSignal to flushAutoCommits — aborting would kill peers' shared-gitRoot flushes). Wrap the flushAutoCommits await (line ~223), the reconcileStatePush call (line ~227, with onTimeout = best-effort abortRebase), and the restoreRetryableRecord call in the shared deadline. At the top of the catch, rethrow RecordDurabilityTimeoutError without restoring. Full before/after snippets are in the PRD (.pan/drafts/PAN-2989.md, WI-1). Tests: new tests/unit/lib/pan-dir/record-update-durability-budget.test.ts with vi.mock('./auto-commit.js') controlling flushAutoCommits and vi.useFakeTimers throughout.

items.title: Given a flushAutoCommits that never resolves, updateIssueRecord rejects with RecordDurabilityTimeoutError after advanceTimersByTimeAsync(30000) and the record lock is immediately acquirable by a second updateIssueRecord call
After a durability timeout the record file on disk still contains the mutation (restoreRetryableRecord is not invoked) and the never-resolving flush promise was not aborted
With OVERDECK_RECORD_DURABILITY_BUDGET_MS=5000, updateIssueRecord rejects with RecordDurabilityTimeoutError at 5000ms instead of the 30000ms default
A flush resolving normally within budget commits, pushes, and returns the updated record exactly as before (no behavior regression on the healthy path)
Scrub agent identity from the spawned dashboard server env

expected_outputs: spawn-env tests pass: server env lacks OVERDECK_AGENT_ID/OVERDECK_ISSUE_ID/OVERDECK_SESSION_TYPE and carries OVERDECK_DASHBOARD_SPAWNED_BY when inherited
port-override guard decision tests pass for conv-*, pipeline-role, and absent identities

narrative.Action: In spawnDashboardDetached (src/cli/commands/restart.ts:182), after applyBootGateEnv: if env.OVERDECK_AGENT_ID is defined copy it to env.OVERDECK_DASHBOARD_SPAWNED_BY, then delete OVERDECK_AGENT_ID, OVERDECK_ISSUE_ID, and OVERDECK_SESSION_TYPE. The env object is built once and flows to both the systemd-unit and plain-spawn paths, so one edit covers both. In src/dashboard/server/config.ts:89 read process.env['OVERDECK_DASHBOARD_SPAWNED_BY'] instead of OVERDECK_AGENT_ID for the nonConversationUsingOverride check — the conv-*/pipeline-role/absent decision table must be byte-for-byte unchanged (NFR-3). Exact snippet in the PRD (.pan/drafts/PAN-2989.md, WI-2).

items.title: Given process.env.OVERDECK_AGENT_ID='deploy-patrol', the env passed to the spawned server contains OVERDECK_DASHBOARD_SPAWNED_BY='deploy-patrol' and none of OVERDECK_AGENT_ID, OVERDECK_ISSUE_ID, OVERDECK_SESSION_TYPE
Given no inherited OVERDECK_AGENT_ID, the spawned server env has no OVERDECK_DASHBOARD_SPAWNED_BY key at all (not the string 'undefined')
The config.ts port-override guard produces identical allow/refuse decisions as before for conv-*, agent-*, and absent spawner identities (unit-tested against OVERDECK_DASHBOARD_SPAWNED_BY)
Proactively drain the workspace verdict fallback

expected_outputs: review-status-record-sync-drain.test.ts passes (newer-journal cleanup, fold-and-delete, clearedFields, retry-schedule cases)

narrative.Action: In src/lib/overdeck/review-status-record-sync.ts: add drainWorkspaceVerdictFallback(issueId) — read the fallback; if absent return true; if the journal record's pipeline.updatedAt is >= fallback.updatedAt delete the file and return true; otherwise call updateIssueRecordForIssue with a ReviewStatus reconstructed from the fallback (cleared fields stay absent so they do not resurrect) and delete the file when the write lands. Wire triggers into updateIssueRecordForReviewStatusSync: on a landed journal write, drain (tracked in pendingJournalWrites so flushReviewStatusJournalWrites covers short-lived CLIs); on a fallback write, scheduleVerdictFallbackDrain with unref'd setTimeout retries at 5s/30s/120s, one timer per issue, stopping on success, exhaustion, or a missing file. Full snippet in the PRD (.pan/drafts/PAN-2989.md, WI-3). Tests use vi.useFakeTimers (repo rule).

items.title: Given a fallback file and a journal already newer than it, drainWorkspaceVerdictFallback deletes the file and performs no record write
Given a fallback newer than the journal, the drain writes the record, deletes the file, and a subsequent readJournalStatusSync returns the record's data with the fallback overlay gone
The drain preserves clearedFields semantics: fields the fallback cleared (e.g. strikeTransportRetryCount) stay absent from the record's pipeline block after the fold
When a journal write fails, the scheduled drain runs at 5s/30s/120s of fake-timer advances, stops after a success, and emits no further attempt after exhaustion
Document the bounded record-lock hold, server-identity scrub, and fallback drain
